Thanks Vanessa — quick technical write-up below to turn into the test checklist. I’ll follow up with diagrams (control-plane-arch.pdf) and an air-gap checklist (airgap-checklist.xlsx).

Short answers / proposed plan:

1) Control plane options:
   - Option 1 (recommended): Customer-managed control plane in Acme VPC using PrivateLink/ENIs. Control plane API endpoints are accessible only from your VPC subnets. We support KMS/HSM integration for customer-managed keys; audit logs are pushed to your CloudWatch/S3 (no data leaves your account). Patch/update cadence is aligned to a scheduled maintenance window you control.
   - Option 2: Redwood-managed control plane with VPC peering & strict IAM roles — slightly faster to onboard but requires careful IAM scoping and some metadata routing through Redwood control plane (we can sign an SLA for access controls).

2) Air-gapped on-prem package:
   - Feasible for most inference workloads. Tradeoffs: no live model catalog; model updates must be delivered via signed bundles. Telemetry is limited (we provide offline log packages and an optional metrics aggregator deployed to a customer-controlled telemetry sink). Some advanced automated eval features are unavailable in fully air-gapped setups.

3) Networking checklist (what we need them to test):
   - Verify outbound access to our private-control-plane endpoint is blocked (we will validate that control-plane traffic uses PrivateLink).
   - Confirm NAT rules for package installation (we can provide an install bundle that is transferred via secure offline media for air-gapped customers).
   - Open outbound ports 443 for secure pulls/updates only if they accept a managed control plane; otherwise no outbound required for fully air-gapped run.

4) Differentiators vs hyperscaler-managed endpoints: 
   - Control plane locality: Redwood can run control plane inside the customer VPC (hyperscaler services often centralize control plane across tenants).
   - Key ownership: KMS/HSM integration with customer keys as default in Dedicated/Private offerings.
   - Consistent runtime: Same inference runtime and optimization across hosted and private deployments; hyperscalers may expose different performance characteristics and limited kernel/customization access.
   - Patch cadence & visibility: You control maintenance windows in customer-managed control plane; hyperscalers push updates across tenants with limited per-tenant scheduling.

Next steps (for EOD tomorrow):
- I’ll produce the two deliverables: control-plane-arch.pdf and an airgap-checklist.xlsx.
- Marissa — can you add the SOC/attestation pointers we should include in the one-pager?
- Vanessa — I’ll draft the feature-delta matrix and the explicit network test commands for Acme’s infra team.

Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
